Finding: DOM nodes and event listeners are retained after repeated SPA route round trips
Evidence: The latest Playwright run recorded identical dashboard slopes of +294 nodes and +2,191 JSEventListeners per cycle: Nodes 1,582 -> 1,876 -> 2,170 -> 2,464; listeners 7,577 -> 9,768 -> 11,959 -> 14,150. A second independent Playwright run reproduced the same slopes; the earlier direct-CDP harness also showed linear retention.
Likely impact: Long user sessions may accumulate detached DOM and listeners, increasing memory use and duplicate handler work.
Recommended action: Profile the home dashboard, patient-registration ESM, and shared shell extensions with Chrome heap snapshots. Check useEffect cleanup, subscriptions, global/window listeners, observers, timers, workspace registration, and AbortControllers on unmount.
Retest / acceptance criterion: Run at least 10 identical round trips with forced GC; node and listener counts should return near each route's warmed baseline instead of increasing linearly.

Finding: Playwright measured forced-GC JavaScript heap growth on every dashboard cycle
Evidence: Latest dashboard JSHeapUsedSize checkpoints: 24,976,520 -> 25,410,500 -> 25,871,264 -> 26,243,024 bytes; total growth 1,266,504 bytes and average growth 422,168 bytes per cycle. The preceding independent run also grew on every cycle by 1,323,636 bytes total.
Likely impact: If the trend continues in longer workflows, browser memory use can climb throughout a clinical session and eventually increase GC pauses or tab instability.
Recommended action: Compare heap snapshots after warm-up and the final cycle, inspect detached DOM retainers, and separate one-time module caching from objects retained on every navigation.
Retest / acceptance criterion: After warm-up, forced-GC heap should plateau across 10-20 cycles while detached-node and listener counts remain stable.

Finding: The authenticated dashboard starts a broad ESM payload
Evidence: Latest uncached Playwright capture: 188 completed requests and 3,241,656 transfer bytes. Scripts account for 139 requests and 2,754,520 transfer bytes (about 85.0% of transferred bytes). The earlier direct-CDP capture measured 14,428,706 decoded bytes.
Likely impact: Slower startup and more parse/compile/main-thread work, especially on low-memory devices or poor links.
Recommended action: Reduce initial ESM activation, defer non-critical extensions, audit shared dependencies, and set performance budgets for initial route scripts.
Retest / acceptance criterion: On an uncached dashboard load, materially reduce total requests and transferred script bytes; track with a fixed-device Lighthouse/CDP budget.

Finding: The login route loads substantial framework and script payload before authentication
Evidence: Latest uncached Playwright capture: 52 completed requests and 1,549,927 transfer bytes. JavaScript accounts for 34 requests and 950,384 transfer bytes; the earlier direct-CDP capture measured 8,747,094 decoded bytes.
Likely impact: Adds delay and CPU work before users can sign in.
Recommended action: Load only login-critical ESMs before authentication; defer devtools, implementer tools, and non-login extensions when they are not required.
Retest / acceptance criterion: Reduce uncached login request count and transferred script bytes without changing sign-in behavior.

Finding: Two hashed shared JavaScript files dominate both login and dashboard transfer
Evidence: Gzip transfer sizes are 288,613 and 275,968 bytes respectively; together they transfer 564,581 bytes.
Likely impact: Large shared chunks delay download, decompression, parsing, and compilation on every cold session.
Recommended action: Generate webpack bundle-analysis reports and source-map-explorer output to identify packages in these chunks; remove duplicate libraries and split login-ineligible code.
Retest / acceptance criterion: No single initial shared chunk should exceed the agreed gzip budget; verify composition in CI.

Finding: Dashboard startup downloads sizeable chunks from adjacent workflow ESMs
Evidence: Observed gzip chunks include express-workflow 108,075 and 53,104 bytes; patient-registration 101,510, 89,204, and 42,928 bytes; patient-search 65,613 and 42,902 bytes.
Likely impact: If these features are not immediately visible, eager activation wastes bandwidth and memory; if visible as extensions, the cost may be intentional.
Recommended action: Map each request to its active page or extension slot. Lazy-load non-visible panels/actions and keep route-only components behind dynamic imports.
Retest / acceptance criterion: Document why every initial-route ESM is active; defer chunks that are not required above the fold.

Finding: A large global stylesheet is part of login and dashboard startup
Evidence: The global stylesheet transfers 200,772 bytes gzip; all three stylesheets total about 228,153 transfer bytes on the dashboard.
Likely impact: CSS download, parse, selector matching, and style recalculation affect initial rendering.
Recommended action: Audit unused Carbon/component CSS, split route-specific styles, and avoid shipping duplicate theme rules across ESMs.
Retest / acceptance criterion: Reduce initial CSS gzip bytes and confirm no visual regressions in login and dashboard screenshots.

Finding: The dashboard makes many small API requests
Evidence: The latest Playwright capture recorded 36 Fetch requests transferring 69,376 bytes, with no dashboard request failures.
Likely impact: Even with a small byte total, request latency and server concurrency can make the page feel slow on high-latency networks.
Recommended action: Identify duplicate or serial requests, share cached session/config data, batch where supported, and avoid fetching data for hidden extensions.
Retest / acceptance criterion: Reduce duplicate/serial fetches and measure route-ready time under realistic network latency.

Finding: The login page requests an image that returns HTTP 404
Evidence: The failed image request was reproduced on each cold login capture.
Likely impact: Wastes one network round trip, creates console/network noise, and may leave a missing visual.
Recommended action: Deploy the referenced file or remove/update the obsolete badge_ksm.png configuration reference.
Retest / acceptance criterion: The login network log contains no 404 for badge_ksm.png.

Finding: The optimized login background is deployed and served successfully
Evidence: HTTP 200; 30,074 transfer bytes in the live QA capture. The earlier static audit found the replaced login-background_ksm.svg at roughly 13 MB.
Likely impact: The oversized login-background transfer hotspot has been removed from QA.
Recommended action: Keep the optimized asset and add an image-size budget so a large SVG cannot be reintroduced.
Retest / acceptance criterion: Login background remains below the agreed byte budget and renders correctly.

Finding: The dashboard has slow LCP, high layout shift, and substantial long-task activity
Evidence: Across two Playwright runs, dashboard LCP was 3,408-4,460 ms and CLS was consistently 0.656. The latest run recorded 18 long tasks totaling 1,866 ms with a longest task of 400 ms. Login LCP was 3,864 ms and CLS was 0.135 in the latest run.
Likely impact: Users can see late content, unstable layout, and delayed interaction, particularly on slower clinic devices.
Recommended action: Trace LCP element discovery and image/font loading, reserve layout space, remove late layout mutations, and profile the long tasks by ESM/function under CPU throttling.
Retest / acceptance criterion: On representative devices, target LCP <= 2,500 ms, CLS <= 0.1, and eliminate avoidable tasks longer than 50 ms.

Finding: The initial dashboard performs substantial script and task work
Evidence: At the latest post-load Playwright baseline, CDP cumulative metrics reported TaskDuration 2.988 seconds, ScriptDuration 1.096 seconds, LayoutDuration 0.041 seconds, and RecalcStyleDuration 0.068 seconds.
Likely impact: Main-thread work can delay interaction on slower clinic devices; totals include work up to the measurement checkpoint.
Recommended action: Capture a Performance trace in a non-sensitive test dataset with CPU throttling, inspect long tasks, and optimize the highest self-time functions and repeated renders.
Retest / acceptance criterion: Under a fixed test profile, reduce long-task count and route-ready CPU time.

Finding: Compression is enabled for the largest text assets
Evidence: The largest JavaScript and CSS responses observed in QA were served with Content-Encoding: gzip.
Likely impact: Compression substantially reduces transfer relative to decoded payload size.
Recommended action: Retain compression and evaluate Brotli for HTTPS static assets if supported by the deployment stack.
Retest / acceptance criterion: Static text assets remain compressed; compare Brotli transfer size and CPU trade-offs before rollout.

Finding: No failed network requests were seen during the authenticated dashboard capture
Evidence: All 188 completed dashboard requests in the latest Playwright run finished without a captured failure.
Likely impact: The tested dashboard path did not show an immediate runtime network reliability problem.
Recommended action: Preserve this baseline and add automated checks for failed critical requests and unhandled errors.
Retest / acceptance criterion: Repeated dashboard smoke tests show zero failed critical requests.
